GOAL: pick one in-scope mechanism for this round that reuses the training behaviour-graph curvature WITHOUT spending codebook radius (CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ's measured failure: kappa_hat=[0.00,-8.96,-25.55] -> code radius [0.0381,0.0312,0.0163], SID 2/13/56, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, Stage3 recall 0.041888).
READ: the round brief (routes a-d, resolution-protection requirement, frozen baseline 247/7414/20223 and 0.055537), plus the prior-round list (CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ, BRad-RQ, CURVCTRL-SID, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID).
OBSERVED: every rejected idea spends the profile on a per-level scalar that sets the SPACE the codes live in (radius, temperature, radial coordinate, cone aperture, Fréchet codebook update). None of them makes the profile a PER-CODE property of the distance chart with the code vectors themselves untouched, and none of them uses a hard equipartition constraint as the resolution guarantee.
REASONING: the measured root cause of the 0.041888 is level-1 utilisation collapse (2 used codes of 256). A mechanism that (i) never touches code norms/radius, (ii) changes the distance chart per code via kappa_{l,k} = kappa_0*exp(alpha*kappa_hat_{l,k}), and (iii) forces hard uniform column marginals in a Sinkhorn assignment, both protects resolution by construction and gives the behaviour curvature a non-degenerate place to act (it can only reorder who goes where, never how many codes exist).
DECISION: propose CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ: per-code chart curvature + entropic balanced transport with uniform marginals; curvature measured on the K-node code-transition quotient graph of the TRAINING split, standardised vs a member-shuffle null, detached, synced every 20 epochs.
OPEN: write the full 22-label block.

GOAL: freeze the final one-idea block for CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ.
READ: nothing new; consolidation of record 2.
OBSERVED: resolved three design questions. (1) Curvature is computed on the K-node CODE quotient graph (K=256 per level) induced by TRAINING transitions under last-synced memberships, not on 256 item subgraphs -> cost is O(E*K) per sync, ran 150 times over the run (every 20 epochs). (2) Resolution protection is the hard uniform Sinkhorn column marginal: every one of the K_l codes receives B/K_l items every step, so level collapse (2 codes) is impossible by construction, and the code vectors keep their inherited parameterisation, norm and count so no radius is spent. (3) The per-code curvature enters only through the distance chart d^_k(x,c)=d_k(x,c)/lambda_k(c) with lambda_k(c)=2/(1-kappa|c|^2), which is exactly the Euclidean distance as kappa->0, so the geometry-off switch is a clean Euclidean balanced assignment and removing geometry also removes the behaviour channel (kappa_hat is multiplied into the metric).
DECISION: ship the block. Predicted per-step overhead: 3 levels x 1023x256 cost entries = 785,664 transcendental evaluations, 8 Sinkhorn sweeps = 6.3M elementwise ops, 3.1 MB extra activations -> +3..6% step time; curvature sync ~150 x 3 x ~5k edge-pairs Ollivier-Sinkhorn -> tens of seconds for the whole 3000-epoch run; one fixed-shape 3x256x256 all_reduce per sync, rank-symmetric, no rank-0-only broadcast, no variable-length transport support.
OPEN: nothing; answer printed.

FINAL ANSWER (shipped): CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ. Per-code chart curvature kappa_{l,k}=kappa_0*exp(alpha*kappa_hat_{l,k}) acts only on a Poincare chart distance dhat_k=d_k/lambda_k(c) inside an entropic transport assignment with HARD uniform column marginals (1/K_l), so code utilisation is pinned at B/K_l by constraint and level collapse (the measured 2/256 that produced 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, recall 0.041888) is impossible by construction; the inherited code table, its norms, counts and init are untouched, so no radius is spent. kappa_hat = clipped 3-sigma standardised Ollivier curvature of the K-node CODE quotient graph built from TRAINING transitions only, under last-synced detached memberships, refreshed every 20 epochs (150 syncs), no gradient, member-shuffle null with 8 shuffles. Coupling: transitions -> quotient curvature -> per-code chart curvature -> cost matrix -> transport plan -> SID token; behaviour-off sets kappa_hat:=0 (uniform curvature, behaviour inert) and geometry-off sets kappa:=0 (Euclidean chart, behaviour inert), so neither acts alone. Cost: 3 levels x 1023 x 256 = 785,664 cost entries/step, 8 Sinkhorn sweeps = 6.3M ops, 3.1 MB extra activations, +3..6% step time, tens of seconds total for the 150 curvature syncs, one fixed-shape [3,256,256] all_reduce per sync (rank-symmetric, no rank-0-only broadcast, no variable-length support). Predicted observables: U_l >= 0.9*K_l, SID counts >= 247/7414/20223, level-1 pos-minus-neg hit gap > 0.02 (baseline 0.002), Stage3 recall target > 0.065 vs frozen 0.055537. Full 22-label block was printed as the response.
